prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_G:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2015 — Summary (≤500 words)

Theme: Stronger Economy, Fairer Society: Opportunity for Everyone.

Key pledges
- Balance the budget fairly by 2017/18 with a mix of spending restraint and taxes on wealth, banks and polluters; allow borrowing for productive investment.
- Cut taxes by raising the Personal Allowance to £12,500; consider aligning employee NI threshold.
- Invest £8bn extra per year in the NHS by 2020; full parity for mental health with new waiting-time standards and £500m extra by 2016/17.
- Protect education funding from nursery to 19; qualified teachers in every class; core national curriculum including PSHE, SRE and financial literacy.
- Five Green Laws (Nature, Zero Carbon Britain, Green Transport, Green Buildings, Resource Efficiency).

Economy and industry
- Long-term industrial strategy; double economy-wide innovation spend; ringfence science budget; expand Catapults and the Green Investment Bank.
- Banking reform to boost competition, community banking and alternative finance; continue Banking Levy.
- Devolve economic powers (transport, housing, skills) via City/Growth Deals; use procurement to support SMEs.
- Green growth: legally binding net zero by 2050; coal out by 2025; power sector decarbonisation target for 2030; expand renewables, storage, CCS; support nuclear without subsidy; community energy.
- Infrastructure: 10‑year plans; HS2 as part of a UK high-speed network; major rail electrification and East‑West Rail; strategic airport policy with no net runway increase; light rail in cities.

Family finances, work, welfare and pensions
- Tough action on avoidance/evasion; High Value Property Levy on homes >£2m.
- Childcare: towards 20 free hours/week for ages 2–4 and from end of parental leave; tax-free childcare; 85% childcare support in UC.
- Complete Universal Credit; improved, devolved back-to-work support; review sanctions; protect disability and carers.
- Fair work: raise/enforce Minimum Wage; pay Living Wage in central government; gender pay transparency; curb abuse of zero-hours; right to request fixed contracts.
- Pensions: make triple lock permanent; complete single-tier pension; auto-enrolment rollout; fairer pension tax relief considered.

Education and youth
- Early years quality uplift; Early Years Pupil Premium to £1,000.
- Stronger school leadership; fair funding formula; inclusive admissions; Ofsted for MATs/LAs; no profit-making state schools.
- Royal College of Teachers; guaranteed QTS; cut workload.
- Double businesses hiring apprentices; expand higher/degree apprenticeships; improve FE funding and parity.
- Extend free school meals to all primary pupils (as resources allow); young person’s 16–21 bus discount.

Health and care
- Integrate health and social care budgets locally by 2018; shift care into community; better GP access; pharmacist-first approach.
- Public health: tobacco levy; minimum unit pricing for alcohol; junk food ad restrictions; air quality plan with Low Emission Zones.
- Carers: £250 annual bonus; paid care leave consult; Carer’s Allowance earnings limit rise.
- Social care: complete care cost cap; raise care workforce standards and pay.

Homes and environment
- Build 300,000 homes/year; at least 10 Garden Cities; public land release; Housing Investment Bank; “Rent to Own”.
- Strengthen tenants’ rights; longer tenancies with predictable rents; ban excessive letting fees; Help to Rent deposit loans.
- Energy efficiency: EPC Band C for all homes by 2035 (fuel-poor and rented by 2027); council tax discount for major upgrades; reform Green Deal into Green Homes Loans.
- Circular economy: 70% recycling by 2020; landfill/incineration reforms; product repairability; resource taxes review.
- Farming: fair supply chains (stronger Groceries Code Adjudicator); animal welfare; TB strategy based on science.

Rights, justice and immigration
- Protect Human Rights Act; Digital Bill of Rights; oppose mass surveillance/Snooper’s Charter; net neutrality.
- Equality: close gender and BAME pay gaps; expand LGBT+ rights; stronger disability rights and accessibility.
- Policing: replace PCCs with Police Boards; victims’ bill; tackle VAWG and teach consent.
- Justice: presumption against short custodial sentences; rehab-focused prisons; drug policy shift to health-led (Portugal model); medicinal cannabis.
- Borders: complete entry/exit checks; faster asylum decisions; allow work after 6 months; separate students in stats; tougher employer enforcement.

Democracy and devolution
- Votes at 16; STV for Westminster and local elections; elected Lords; cap donations at £10k; constitutional convention; Home Rule for Scotland and Wales; Devolution on Demand in England; fair funding with a Welsh floor.

International
- Strongly pro‑EU with reform; support TTIP with protections; in/out referendum only with material treaty change.
- Meet 0.7% aid; lead on SDGs; climate leadership and global conservation.
- Defence: SDSR-based Single Security Budget; modernise forces; step down nuclear posture (end continuous patrols); strengthen cyber and European cooperation.

TEXT_D:
UKIP Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core stance
- Leave the EU to regain sovereignty, control borders, laws and trade; hold an immediate in/out referendum (British citizens only), prefer Article 50 exit. Seek a bespoke UK–EU free-trade deal and wider global FTAs; maintain cooperation on security, health and science agencies. Establish a Post‑EU Secretariat to unwind EU law.

Public finances and tax
- Fund plans by: saving £9bn net EU contributions; cutting foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI; scrapping HS2; replacing the Barnett Formula with a needs‑based system; ending “health tourism”; and cutting government/quangos.
- Tax: raise personal allowance to at least £13,000 (no income tax on minimum wage); introduce a 30% band between £43.5k–£55k; raise the 40% threshold to £55k; abolish inheritance tax; increase transferable allowance for married/civil partners; cut small business rates (20% relief under £50k rateable value). Close multinational avoidance; restore UK tax sovereignty.

NHS and social care
- Extra £12bn over five years; 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GP pilots in A&E; £1.5bn for mental health/dementia; free hospital parking; end PFI; replace CQC/Monitor with elected county health boards; scrap EU Clinical Trials and Working Time directives; exclude NHS from TTIP. Social care: restore funding to 2010 levels (+£1.2bn/yr), integrate with NHS, dignity code, abolish 15‑minute visits, increase Carer’s Allowance by £572/yr; explore shale-funded sovereign wealth fund for care cap.

Immigration and borders
- End EU free movement; Australian-style points system; five‑year moratorium on unskilled immigration; +2,500 Border Agency staff; strict visas; five years’ tax/NI before access to benefits and most NHS care; no amnesty for illegal migrants; deport foreign criminals; revoke citizenship for terrorists by law change. EU citizens resident at referendum may remain and apply for citizenship after five years.

Welfare, pensions, families
- Tighter benefit cap and fraud action; scrap bedroom tax; pay Housing Benefit to under‑25s; reform disability assessments via GPs/specialists; fund 800 advisers in foodbanks. Flexible state pension window; expand pensions guidance; criminalise pension cold‑calling; restore lifelong war widows’ pensions. Childcare: deregulate to expand places and cut costs; statutory wrap‑around care (8am–6pm).

Education and skills
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; expand grammar and vocational/technical schools with later transfer tests; apprenticeships can replace four non‑core GCSEs; rework GCSE tiers; keep AS as standalone; first‑aid in PSHE; reverse special-school closures; refocus Ofsted. Waive tuition fees for UK STEMM/Medicine students who work and pay tax in UK for five years.

Housing and environment
- Prioritise brownfield (register, remediation grants, stamp duty relief up to £250k); bring empty homes back; build 1m on brownfield by 2025; protect green belt; local referendums on large schemes; “local connection” priority for social housing; restrict Right to Buy/Help to Buy to British citizens (armed forces exception for non‑British on RTB). Homelessness register.

Transport and energy
- Scrap HS2; consider Manston airport; limit speed cameras to safety; oppose road pricing/eCall; end most tolls; double HGV levy for foreign trucks; VED exemption for 25+‑year vehicles. Repeal Climate Change Act; end wind/solar subsidies and green levies/ETS; back hydro, nuclear, gas, shale (with safeguards and sovereign wealth fund), and coal (new efficient plants, end EU combustion directives); cut prepayment penalties.

Jobs, business and trade
- Prioritise British workers; curb EURES/relocation grants; enforce minimum wage; regulate zero‑hours abuses. Help SMEs: rate relief, crackdown on late payments (HMRC fines), pilot trade credit insurance, 30‑minute free town‑centre parking, cut EU red tape, open public contracts.

Farming, fishing, heritage
- New Single Farm Payment (£80/acre, capped), support dairy/sheep, tougher animal welfare, ban live exports, enable small abattoirs. Leave CFP; UK 12‑mile and 200‑mile EEZ; rebuild stocks; favour under‑10m fleet; protect anglers. Create Heritage/Tourism minister; remove VAT on listed‑building repairs; “seaside town status”; save pubs (micro-brewery tax breaks, optional ventilated smoking rooms, oppose alcohol minimum pricing, reverse tobacco plain packs).

Crime, justice, defence, culture
- 6,000 extra posts across police, prisons and borders; review constabulary structure/PCCs; invest in tech; decriminalise TV licence non‑payment. Leave ECHR jurisdiction; repeal HRA; UK Bill of Rights; end European Arrest Warrant. Defence: spend ≥2% GDP (rising by up to £4bn by 2020), retain Trident, restore capabilities, carriers in service, review F‑35, create Director of National Intelligence, oppose EU army; no income tax on active service. Promote British culture, integration and English language; add St George’s and St David’s Day bank holidays.

Overseas aid
- Cut to 0.2% of GNI; focus on emergencies, vaccinations, clean water/sanitation; merge DFID into FCO; “trade not aid,” prefer UK providers.
